name: Early Repolarization Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Criteria for Early Repolarization Syndrome

criteria.description: J-point elevation ≥0.1 mV in at least two contiguous inferior and/or lateral leads on ECG
Presence of slurring or notching of the terminal QRS complex
No evidence of structural heart disease on imaging
History of idiopathic ventricular fibrillation or unexplained sudden cardiac arrest
Family history of sudden cardiac death under age 50

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: J-point elevation with slurring or notching in at least two contiguous leads plus absence of structural heart disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of J-point elevation and structural heart disease.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic ECG finding defining the syndrome
Distinctive ECG morphology associated with early repolarization

common.notes: Life-threatening arrhythmia associated with the syndrome
Transient loss of consciousness due to arrhythmia
Sudden cardiac arrest often occurring during sleep

rare.notes: Abnormal breathing pattern preceding cardiac arrest
searchTerms: nocturnal choking or struggling to breathe

rare.symptomName: Seizure-like activity secondary to cerebral hypoxia
rare.notes: Convulsive syncope due to arrhythmia-induced hypoxia
searchTerms: seizure-like episodes from low brain oxygen

imaging: Normal echocardiogram excluding structural heart disease
genetic: Mutations in genes related to cardiac ion channels (e.g., KCNJ8, CACNA1C)
other: Characteristic ECG pattern with J-point elevation and terminal QRS notching/slurring

distinguishingFeatures: ST-segment elevation in right precordial leads (V1-V3)
Higher risk of ventricular arrhythmias localized to right ventricular outflow tract
Associated chest pain and pericardial rub
Localized ST-segment elevation with reciprocal changes
Regional wall motion abnormalities on imaging

redFlags: Family history of sudden cardiac death under age 50
Documented ventricular fibrillation or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
references: Haïssaguerre M, et al. 'Sudden cardiac arrest associated with early repolarization.' N Engl J Med. 2008.
Antzelevitch C, et al. 'J-wave syndromes expert consensus conference report.' Heart Rhythm. 2017.
Tikkanen JT, et al. 'Long-term outcome associated with early repolarization on electrocardiography.' N Engl J Med. 2009.
